chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: The battle of the bands against Nat Towles at Dreamland
summary: One night at the Dreamland Ballroom in Omaha Hunter's swinging band beat Nat Towles's better-arranged band because of its drummer.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Gus, we started to talk about the battle that the two bands had, Lloyd Hunter and Nat Towles at the Dreamland Ballroom in Omaha.
Well, that was some night, huh? It was one night?
Well, Nat came to town and he'd been in town for about a couple of months. And so I found out that we were supposed to play a battle against him. And at this time I was playing drums.
So we had another new bass player with us. It was the same bass player that -- when I first came to Omaha, Nebraska Basie, we called him.
Yeah, he was in the six-piece band.
And a very good bass player.
So we had this battle at Dreamland Ballroom.
Yeah. Check this back, Gus, and make sure we're doing all right.
Good. So this is the night that's going to be the battle.

This is the night of the battle. So we played first, Lloyd Hunter's band. And after we played, did our numbers, then Nat Towles came on. And when Nat came on, he had all these good arrangements and these good musicians, but that band just didn't swing on account of the drummer.
So I knew I had him beat right there, you see.
And everybody loved the band, they loved Nat's band.
But they were playing for dancing, though.
We got the biggest applause, on account of --
It just didn't swing like Lloyd's band.
Lloyd had a good swing band, very good swing band.
And Nat Towles, he had good numbers and everything. But he just didn't have that beat.
The bass player really carried Nat Towles' band.
Yeah. Well, you can't get anywhere if you don't have a good drummer in the band.
Oh, sure, that's the way it is.
And worse when you got a bad drummer in the band.
But -- turn it off just a second.
All right, so, okay, you were sitting pretty then, because --
Oh, I was sitting pretty then.
So we whipped them real good that night.
And they never had another battle against us.
They were kind of dragged, I guess.
Yeah, they was talking about the drummer. I said, 'Oh, he did good, I thought, myself.' Quite naturally, I'm going to stick up for him.
Yeah, right. He had good competition.
